title: Define “minimum supported” observability pack for Redwood Private (dashboards, alerts, logs) + acceptance criteria and rollout plan
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
content:
## Summary
We need a clear, supportable definition of the “minimum supported” observability experience for **Redwood Private** (VPC + on-prem). This ticket defines:
- What we ship by default (dashboards, alert rules, log pipeline)
- What “supported” means (and what is explicitly out of scope)
- Acceptance criteria for v1
- Rollout plan and enablement requirements (Support/SRE readiness)

This definition is used by Engineering (Telemetry/Private Deployments), SRE, Solutions/PS, and Support as the contract for Private installs.

## Background / Why now
Private customers consistently ask:
- “What do I get out of the box for monitoring?”
- “Which dashboards/alerts are supported by Redwood Support?”
- “How do I export logs to my SIEM in an air-gapped environment?”

We’ve also seen recurring support cases where:
- Dashboards are missing/blank after install or upgrade
- Prometheus scrapes fail due to NetworkPolicy changes
- Alert rules are noisy with default thresholds

We will standardize the baseline and ship it as a versioned bundle via Helm + private installer.

## Definition: Minimum Supported Observability Pack (v1)
### Supported baseline (what Redwood ships + supports)
**A) Metrics + Dashboards (Grafana)
**We ship a curated set of **versioned Grafana dashboards** under an explicit “Redwood Private / Minimum Pack” folder. The dashboards are expected to render against the shipped recording rules and bounded-cardinality metrics.

Must-have dashboards (v1):
1) **Runtime Overview (Serving runtime)**
   - Request rate (RPS) and token throughput
   - p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end + runtime processing)
   - Error rate by class (4xx/5xx, timeouts, upstream)
   - Batching/queueing indicators (queue depth, batch size, queue wait)
   - GPU utilization + memory pressure (where available)
   - KV cache indicators (hit rate / reuse where instrumented)

2) **Control Plane Health**
   - API gateway health (availability, latency)
   - Routing/policy engine health
   - Auth/RBAC integration points (error rate/timeouts)
   - Installer/upgrade controller status and recent reconciles

3) **Infrastructure / Kubernetes Signals (minimum view)**
   - Pod restarts / CrashLoopBackOff for Redwood namespaces
   - Node pressure (CPU/memory), PVC usage for Prometheus/Grafana/log collector
   - Prometheus scrape health summary (targets up/down, scrape errors)

Nice-to-have (explicitly not required for v1 support):
- Deep per-model performance breakdowns beyond bounded aggregates
- Multi-cluster federated views
- Customer-specific custom panels maintained by Redwood

**B) Alerting (Prometheus alert rules)
**We ship a minimal set of alert rules aligned to Private SLO guidance. Alerts must include:
- Severity taxonomy (page vs ticket)
- Clear annotations with “what to do first”
- Runbook link (internal + customer-facing where appropriate)

Minimum alert categories (v1):
1) **SLO / Golden signal alerts**
   - API availability SLO burn (fast + slow burn)
   - Latency SLO burn (p95 and/or p99 depending on endpoint)
   - Elevated error rate (5xx + timeouts) with suppression for planned maintenance windows

2) **Saturation / resource pressure (inference-critical)**
   - GPU saturation sustained
   - OOM kills / CUDA OOM (or container OOMKilled)
   - CPU throttling / memory pressure for runtime pods (sustained)
   - Queue depth / backpressure sustained (where available)

3) **Platform health**
   - CrashLoopBackOff/restart loops for core control plane + runtime
   - Prometheus scrape target down (Redwood services) beyond grace window
   - Prometheus TSDB disk filling / PVC high watermark
   - Grafana unhealthy (service down)

Alerting defaults:
- **Paging** only for conditions that imply customer-visible outage or imminent outage.
- Everything else defaults to **ticket / non-page** to avoid “noisy by default” installs.
- Customers can opt into more aggressive paging thresholds, but Redwood Support will treat those as customer-configured.

**C) Logs (structured, safe-by-default) + export options
**We ship a supported **log collection and forwarding configuration** for Redwood namespaces.

Log content requirements:
- Structured JSON logs for core services
- Required fields (where applicable): `timestamp`, `level`, `service`, `component`, `cluster_id`, `namespace`, `pod`, `request_id`, `route` (bounded), `model` (bounded/normalized), `status_code`, `latency_ms`
- Tenant identifier must be **hashed** (no raw tenant/customer identifiers)
- **No prompt or completion payloads** in operational logs by default
- Explicit redaction rules for tokens/secrets/credentials

Supported sinks/export (v1):
- **Loki** (Grafana ecosystem)
- **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch**
- **Splunk HEC**
- **OTLP logs** export is optional for v1 (documented if low-risk; not required for GA support)

Retention defaults (v1 guidance):
- Metrics: 15 days (configurable)
- Logs: 7 days locally (configurable), with recommendation to export to customer SIEM for longer retention

### What “Supported” means (contract)
If a customer deploys Redwood Private using the installer/Helm charts with the minimum pack enabled **without unsupported modifications**, Redwood Support/SRE will:
- Troubleshoot missing dashboards and alert behavior using the shipped runbooks
- Validate data availability (scrapes, recording rules, datasource)
- Provide recommended tuning for thresholds where documented

Not supported under “minimum pack”:
- Maintaining bespoke dashboards created by the customer
- Debugging third-party Prometheus operator variants with significant customization (we can provide best-effort guidance)
- Long retention or advanced compliance configurations beyond documented knobs
- Full-fidelity distributed tracing across all internal hops (v1)

## Requirements / Non-goals
### Must-haves (v1)
- Turnkey installation via Helm/installer with sane defaults
- Works in air-gapped/on-prem packaging (dashboards + rules + images bundled/versioned)
- Bounded metrics cardinality (no unbounded `route`, `model`, `tenant_id`, `request_id` labels in Prometheus series)
- Backward-compatible upgrades OR a documented migration path (dashboards/alerts should not silently break)
- Runbooks linked directly from alert annotations
- Security review sign-off for log fields + retention guidance

### Non-goals (v1)
- Multi-cluster observability federation
- Premium features: long retention, advanced tracing sampling controls, per-customer dashboard customization
- Building a new SIEM (we export to the customer’s tools)

## Acceptance Criteria
The minimum pack is considered defined and ready for GA when all items below are true.

### Functional acceptance
1) **Dashboards render** out-of-the-box in reference environments (VPC + on-prem-like) and show non-empty panels after running basic traffic.
2) **Prometheus alerts** load successfully and fire under controlled failure injection (e.g., scrape down, pod restart loops, forced latency).
3) **Logs are collected** from Redwood namespaces and can be exported to at least one supported sink (Loki OR Splunk HEC OR Elasticsearch) using documented examples.
4) **Installer/Helm wiring**: minimum pack can be enabled/disabled with a single top-level values switch; key knobs (retention, scrape intervals, sink config) are documented.
5) **Air-gapped packaging**: offline bundle includes all required artifacts (dashboards, rules, collector config, images) with version pinning.

### Supportability acceptance
6) Every page-worthy alert includes:
   - impact statement
   - immediate checks (“what to do first”)
   - runbook URL
   - ownership (team/service)
7) Known issues documented with workarounds (dashboards blank, scrape blocked by NetworkPolicy, alert noise tuning).
8) Sizing guidance published (Prometheus/Grafana/log collector CPU/mem/PVC) for at least 3 footprint tiers.

### Security/compliance acceptance
9) Security sign-off that operational logs do not include secrets/PII by default; redaction guidance included.
10) Clear guidance on audit logs vs operational logs, with retention recommendations.

## Rollout Plan
### Phase 0 — Internal dogfood (staging/private reference)
- Enable minimum pack by default in Redwood-managed reference clusters.
- Run smoke tests on every build that touches installer/Helm/observability-pack.
- Success gate: dashboards stable across 2 upgrades + 1 rollback test.

### Phase 1 — Design partners (opt-in)
- Select 2–4 Private customers (mix of VPC + on-prem/air-gap) with Solutions involvement.
- Default remains **off** for existing installs unless explicitly enabled.
- Weekly alert noise review with SRE (tune thresholds and disable non-actionable alerts by default).
- Success gate: Support can resolve “no dashboards / scrape down / log export auth” issues using runbooks without engineering intervention in >80% of cases.

### Phase 2 — GA (supported minimum)
- Ship as “Minimum Supported Observability Pack” in release notes.
- Default **on for new installs**; existing installs prompted during upgrade with a migration note.
- Support readiness checklist complete (on-call playbooks, known issues, escalation paths).

### Phase 3 — Post-GA hardening
- Track top 5 support drivers and iterate (dashboards, alert noise, export configs).
- Evaluate OTLP logs/traces as a first-class supported sink for v2.

## Metrics of success
- Reduce time-to-triage for Private incidents (target: -30% median from support ticket open to first actionable diagnosis)
- Reduce “missing/blank dashboards” support cases (target: -50% QoQ)
- Keep alert noise within acceptable levels (page rate aligns to SLO impact; no default paging for non-outage signals)

## Open Questions
1) Do we require OTLP logs export as a supported sink for v1, or treat it as “documented best-effort”?
2) Do we ship Prometheus/Grafana (batteries included) or integrate with customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana as the primary path?
   - Current direction: ship integration + defaults; allow customer-managed as supported if they meet documented prerequisites.
3) What is the minimum set of runtime-specific recording rules needed to keep dashboards stable while bounding cardinality?

## Updates
### 2025-05-22 (Vivek)
Aligned with Neha/Sean on “page vs ticket” philosophy: only SLO burn + imminent outage conditions page by default. Added explicit non-goals for premium observability.

### 2025-06-05 (Vivek)
Confirmed air-gap requirement: bundle must include dashboards/rules/config + checksums, and installer must validate presence of artifacts preflight.

### 2025-06-27 (Vivek)
Reviewed early alert noise feedback from staging: CPU/memory thresholds too tight; default rules should target sustained saturation + correlate with error rate where possible.

### 2025-07-18 (Vivek)
Definition finalized for GA readiness. Engineering work tracked in ENG sub-issues; Support enablement and known-issues doc required before default-on for new installs.
